name: Sprocket
text: We should auto-apply safe, high-confidence improvements to our prompts and routing rules. This cuts review time and keeps the system evolving without manual bottlenecks. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of misapplied changes—mitigated by strict safety checks and rollback paths. The artifact is a documented auto-apply pipeline with clear thresholds for "safe."

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t misapplied changes—it’s *silent drift*: auto-applied tweaks that subtly shift system behavior over time, making failures harder to trace. A better alternative is a staged rollout: auto-apply only to non-critical paths first, with human review on every 10th change. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot on 5% of traffic and measuring error rate deltas against the baseline.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: The real risk is *cascading context loss*: auto-applied tweaks to non-critical paths can subtly alter how downstream systems interpret inputs, creating failures that only surface when critical paths break. A better alternative is a *shadow mode* where changes run in parallel for a week before auto-applying—settle it by running a controlled experiment with synthetic failures injected to measure drift before full rollout.
